about.title: About Ink & Page
about.description: A practical PDF workspace for signing, combining and organizing documents in your browser.

sections.heading: Finishing touches without a complicated workflow
paragraphs: Ink & Page brings everyday PDF tasks into one browser workspace: add a visual signature or stamp, arrange pages, merge files, extract a section, create page images and prepare a final download. The aim is to make the work around a document easier to understand, with a visible preview and controls that explain their effect.

The editor is designed for documents you already have. It does not verify a signer's identity, issue signing certificates, replace a full word processor or promise accurate conversion of scanned pages into editable text.

sections.heading: What stays on your device
paragraphs: The shipped PDF tools read selected files and process document contents in your browser. They do not send PDF contents, signatures or stamps to a document-processing server. Opening the website still involves requests to its hosting provider, and downloading a result saves a new file through your browser.

The active editor document stays in memory. The merge workspace intentionally retains source files and their arrangement in this browser's IndexedDB storage so a refresh can restore your work. Reusable signatures are saved only when you opt in. Browser storage is not a secure vault and should be cleared on shared devices.

sections.heading: Clear limits, honest results
paragraphs: Some encrypted PDFs can be displayed by the viewer but cannot be copied directly into a new PDF. Recovery exports those pages as images and reports the tradeoff: their appearance is retained, while text selection and interactive elements are not. PDFs that require an opening password must be unlocked by their authorized owner first.

Ink & Page has no advertising or analytics enabled in this release. Operator identity and a verified support contact have not yet been configured; the Contact page explains this rather than displaying an invented address.

contact.title: Contact & support
contact.description: Troubleshooting steps and an honest explanation of Ink & Page's current contact options.

sections.heading: Support contact is not configured yet
paragraphs: The site owner has not supplied a verified public support email or configured a message-delivery service. There is no working contact form on this page, and no email address is implied. Please do not enter confidential documents or personal details into an unrelated form expecting them to reach Ink & Page.

Owner setup required: publish a monitored support email and a privacy contact before presenting this service as having a direct support channel. The public operator or business name can be added when verified. This notice is deliberately visible until those details are provided.

sections.heading: When a PDF will not export
paragraphs: Keep the original files. Record which tool failed, the browser name and version, the approximate document size, and the complete error message. A screenshot of the controls can help explain the issue, but remove confidential page contents before sharing it.

Refresh to load the current website version. For a merge that cannot copy a source PDF normally, try Compatibility mode and review the image-export notice. If the document asks for an opening password, obtain an unlocked copy from its authorized owner. Do not use Remove everything as an export troubleshooting step unless you intend to clear that saved workspace.

sections.heading: For privacy or deletion questions
paragraphs: Remove PDF clears the current editor document. Saved merge files and reusable signatures have separate deletion controls because they are different kinds of browser data. Clear all local data is intended for clearing the site's stored workspace on the device you are using. It does not delete source PDFs or downloads from your computer.

If a future support address is configured, send the minimum detail needed to describe a problem. Do not send signatures, identity records or complete confidential files unless you have a clear reason and an appropriate way to share them.

privacy-policy.title: Privacy policy
privacy-policy.description: How Ink & Page processes PDFs, stores local workspaces and handles browser data.

sections.heading: Scope and last update
paragraphs: Last updated: 19 November 2026. This page describes the features shipped with this browser-based version of Ink & Page. It is an operational description, not a promise of absolute confidentiality or a substitute for an organization's document-handling policy.

The site owner has not yet configured a verified public operator name or privacy contact. See Contact for the current status. This policy should be reviewed and completed by the owner before adding services that collect personal information.

sections.heading: PDF and image processing
paragraphs: Selected PDFs, images, signatures and stamps are read and processed locally by JavaScript running in your browser. The tools do not upload document contents to a processing backend. Output files are generated locally and offered as browser downloads. The website and bundled resources are delivered by the hosting provider, which necessarily receives ordinary connection information when a page is requested.

The active document in the signature/editor workspace is held in memory and is not automatically persisted as the active editor PDF. Replacing or removing it clears its document-specific editing state. Closing or refreshing the page can discard that active editing work.

sections.heading: Persistent merge workspace
paragraphs: The merge workspace stores source-file bytes, grouping and page order in IndexedDB under this site's origin, including the ink-page database. This allows the workspace to return after a refresh on the same browser profile. It is separate from the original files on your device.

The data remains until you clear the merge workspace, use Clear all local data, clear the site's browser storage, or the browser removes it because of storage limits or other browser behavior. There is no fixed server retention period because this feature does not store the files on an Ink & Page server.

sections.heading: Reusable signatures
paragraphs: Saving reusable signatures or stamp images is optional. If you opt in, the library is stored in this browser's IndexedDB storage. Older versions used localStorage; a migration reads those legacy assets and transfers them without intentionally discarding your saved images. The storage controls let you delete individual saved assets or forget the library.

Browser-local storage is not described as encrypted-at-rest storage. Someone who can use your unlocked browser profile may be able to access saved assets. On a shared or public computer, leave signature saving off and clear saved workspace data when finished.

sections.heading: Cookies, analytics and advertising
paragraphs: This release does not enable a third-party analytics service, live AdSense code or advertising requests. Local storage used for workspace features is explained in the Cookie policy. No advertising consent is assumed to have been granted.

If advertising, analytics or a support backend is added later, the owner must update these disclosures and configure any applicable consent and retention controls before activating it. Prepared integration code is not the same as an active service.

sections.heading: Control, security and limitations
paragraphs: Use Remove PDF for the current editor document, the merge removal controls for the retained merge list, Forget saved images for reusable assets, or Clear all local data for this site's saved workspace. Deleting site data does not remove PDFs already downloaded to your computer. You can also use your browser's site-data settings.

Keep originals and inspect downloaded results. Processing may fail for malformed files, unsupported features or browser memory limits. A visual signature is an image or text mark, not identity verification or a cryptographic signing service. Your own rights to access, share and modify a document remain your responsibility.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.description: Practical terms for using Ink & Page's browser-based PDF tools.

sections.heading: Draft terms and service scope
paragraphs: Last updated: 19 November 2026. These terms are a general draft for the current website and should receive legal review. The owner has not supplied a verified legal operator name, business address or public contact. No jurisdiction-specific dispute arrangement is represented as finalized.

Ink & Page provides tools for creating a new PDF or image output from files you select. Features and availability may change. No account, paid plan, document-processing backend or support-delivery service is provided in this release.

sections.heading: Your documents and authority
paragraphs: Use the tools only for documents you are entitled to access and modify. Obtain permission before adding another person's signature or stamp, sharing confidential material, or altering a document that carries contractual, regulatory or professional significance.

Do not use the service to impersonate a person, forge authorization, conceal unlawful activity, distribute malicious files or infringe another party's rights. Possession of a signature image does not establish permission to sign on that person's behalf.

sections.heading: Review every result
paragraphs: Keep an original copy and check page order, missing pages, image clarity, numbers and signature placement before relying on a download. PDF formats vary, and the output may not preserve every interactive feature, annotation, font or original signature validation state.

A visual signature added by these tools is not a certificate-based digital signature, legal identity check or guarantee that a document satisfies a particular signing requirement. Editing a previously digitally signed PDF may invalidate that signature. Compatibility and compression exports can flatten pages into images, reducing text selection and interactive behavior.

sections.heading: Availability and responsibility
paragraphs: The tools are provided without a promise that every file can be processed or that the service will be continuously available. The website cannot guarantee a particular file size, compression result, browser performance, regulatory outcome or suitability for a specialized workflow.

Nothing here limits rights that cannot lawfully be excluded. The owner should complete the legal identity, contact, warranty and liability wording with qualified advice appropriate to the service and its users before treating this draft as final legal documentation.

sections.heading: Local storage and future changes
paragraphs: Some workspaces are retained in this browser to support continued editing. Read Privacy policy and Cookie policy to understand what persists and how to clear it. Browser storage may be lost or inaccessible; it is not a backup service.
Any future advertising, analytics, paid features or server processing must be described before it is activated. These terms do not authorize charges, subscriptions or third-party account changes.

cookie-policy.title: Cookies & browser storage
cookie-policy.description: What Ink & Page saves locally and how to clear it.

sections.heading: Current behavior
paragraphs: Last updated: 19 November 2026. The shipped tools use browser storage to retain selected workspace features. The application does not enable advertising cookies or a third-party analytics service. A cookie banner is not used to suggest that advertising consent has been granted.

IndexedDB and localStorage are browser storage mechanisms, not the same thing as cookies. They still require clear explanation because they can retain file contents, settings or reusable images on the device.

sections.heading: Merge files and reusable assets
paragraphs: The merge workspace retains source bytes and page arrangements in the site's ink-page IndexedDB database so a refresh can restore the list. This is enabled by the merge workflow and should be treated as persistent local document storage.

Reusable signature and stamp images are stored only after you opt in. The current library uses IndexedDB. Legacy localStorage assets are read for migration to avoid silent data loss. Any preference storage is used for the visible workspace behavior rather than cross-site advertising.
The optional light/dark theme selection is saved in localStorage under ink-theme. Clear all local data removes that preference as well.

sections.heading: Deleting local data
paragraphs: Use the application's separate controls to remove the active PDF, clear the saved merge workspace, forget reusable signatures, or clear all local data. A confirmation is shown for clearing saved workspace data. Browser site-data settings can also remove this origin's storage.

Clearing browser storage does not delete source files or completed downloads from your computer. It may remove work that has not been exported. On a shared device, review both the site's stored data and the browser's Downloads folder before handing the device to someone else.

sections.heading: If tracking or ads are added later
paragraphs: Advertising and analytics are disabled in this release. Before activation, the owner must identify the actual services, update this policy and the privacy policy, and implement consent where required. For personalized Google ads in the EEA, UK and Switzerland, a properly configured Google-certified consent platform integrated with the IAB TCF is required.

A future consent interface must let users make a real choice and must not mark consent as granted by default. Prepared ad placeholders do not create a right to activate ads without the owner's approval and correct account settings.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Answers about PDF editing, local storage, signatures, encrypted files and export quality.

sections.heading: Know what the tools do
paragraphs: These answers describe the current browser-based tools. For a task-specific walkthrough, open a guide and follow its link to the working tool. Keep an original file and inspect the result before sharing it.

faq.q: Are my PDFs uploaded to a processing server?
faq.a: No. The shipped PDF tools process selected file contents in your browser. The site itself is delivered by a hosting provider, which receives ordinary page-request information. This local-processing design is not a guarantee against access by someone using your unlocked device.

faq.q: Will a refresh keep my work?
faq.a: The active editor PDF is held in memory and can be lost on refresh. The merge workspace is different: it retains source bytes and page arrangement in IndexedDB so the list can be restored in the same browser. Reusable signatures are saved only when you opt in.

faq.q: How do I remove a document without refreshing?
faq.a: Use Remove PDF in the editor's document toolbar. If unsaved document edits exist, review the confirmation. Replace PDF lets you choose another file. These actions are separate from clearing the saved merge list or all local data.

faq.q: Does adding a signature create a legally verified electronic signature?
faq.a: The tool adds a visual mark, such as a drawn, typed or uploaded signature image. It does not verify identity, create a certificate-based digital signature or guarantee compliance with a particular legal signing process.

faq.q: Can I keep a signature for next time?
faq.a: Yes, if you explicitly enable saving. The reusable library is stored in this browser's IndexedDB storage, and legacy saved assets are migrated. You can forget individual assets or the saved library. Avoid saving sensitive signatures on a shared computer.

faq.q: Why did some merged pages become images?
faq.a: A PDF may display correctly but contain encrypted or incompatible internal objects that cannot be copied directly. Recovery renders affected pages from the local preview and reports the count. Their visual appearance is retained, but text selection and interactive fields on those pages are not.

faq.q: Can the tools open a password-protected PDF?
faq.a: A file that requires an opening password needs an unlocked copy from its authorized owner before use. Some encrypted PDFs open without asking for a password; those can use the compatibility recovery workflow. The site does not bypass passwords.

faq.q: What are the file limits?
faq.a: The configured limits are 100 MB per file, up to 1,500 pages and 400 MB of merge input. A device may run out of memory before reaching those limits, especially with scanned documents or high-resolution image exports. Work in smaller batches if necessary.

faq.q: Can I extract pages without changing their quality?
faq.a: For a PDF that supports direct copying, extraction preserves the original PDF page contents and selectable text where present. If compatibility rendering is needed, the result becomes image-based instead. Check the export notice and inspect the download.

faq.q: How do page ranges work?
faq.a: Use individual pages and inclusive ranges such as 1,3-5,last. Page references start at 1. Check the selected page preview and output order before downloading. A range outside the document's page count is rejected.

faq.q: Can I turn a scan into searchable text?
faq.a: Not in this release. Text export reads an existing PDF text layer. Scanned or image-only PDFs need OCR, which is not implemented. PDF-to-Word and PDF-to-Excel conversion are also not offered as working tools.

faq.q: Will compression always make a PDF smaller?
faq.a: No. Image-based compression renders pages with selected quality and resolution settings. It may reduce a large scan, but can increase a compact text PDF. It also flattens page contents and makes text non-selectable. Compare the before-and-after sizes and inspect readability.

faq.q: Can I number only part of a document?
faq.a: Yes. Use the numbering page-range and exclusion controls, set a starting number, choose a position and font size, and inspect the preview. Document page numbers and the numbering value you print are different, so check the first numbered page carefully.

faq.q: Which browsers should I use?
faq.a: Use an up-to-date Chrome, Chromium-based Edge or Firefox. The bundled PDF.js legacy build targets Chrome 125 and later, with Safari 18 and later mostly supported upstream. Actual feature behavior can vary, and older browsers may need an update.

faq.q: What happens to an existing digital signature?
faq.a: Editing or rebuilding a digitally signed PDF may invalidate its original cryptographic signature. A visible signature image can remain on a page even when validation no longer succeeds. Keep the original and use an appropriate certificate-signing workflow when validation matters.

faq.q: Is there a support inbox or live advertising?
faq.a: A verified public support address has not been configured, and this release has no live ads or analytics. The Contact page states that limitation. AdSense preparation does not mean Google has approved the site or that ads have been activated.

guides.title: Practical PDF guides
guides.description: Clear instructions for signing, stamping, merging, splitting, numbering and creating PDFs from images.

sections.heading: Choose the finishing task
paragraphs: Start with the result you need: a visible signature, a repeatable stamp, one combined file, a smaller page selection, numbered pages or an image collection packaged as a PDF. Each guide explains the inputs, the main controls and the checks to make before sharing a download.

Keep an original copy. PDF formats can contain forms, annotations, unusual page sizes and existing digital signatures. A successful download should still be opened and reviewed, especially when a compatibility or compression notice says that pages were flattened into images.

sections.heading: Six hands-on walkthroughs
paragraphs: How to sign a PDF explains drawing, typing and uploading a visual mark. How to add a stamp covers reusable images, ranges and consistent placement. How to merge PDFs covers source order and recovery. How to split PDF pages helps you extract or package sections. How to number PDF pages separates document page positions from printed numbering. How to convert images to PDF covers page size, orientation, fit and margins.

sections.heading: Privacy while you work
paragraphs: The tools process document contents in the browser. The merge workspace retains files locally to survive a refresh; the active editor document is held in memory. Saving reusable signatures is optional. Read Privacy policy before using a shared device or handling documents subject to an organization's own data rules.

guides/sign-pdf.title: How to add a visual signature to a PDF
guides/sign-pdf.description: Draw, type or upload a signature, position it accurately and export a new PDF.

sections.heading: Prepare a document and a mark
paragraphs: Use a copy of the PDF you intend to sign. Decide whether a visual mark is suitable for your workflow: Ink & Page does not perform identity verification or certificate-based signing. If a document must retain a validated digital signature, keep its original and check the required signing process before editing.
A transparent PNG is useful for an uploaded signature because it avoids covering page text with a white rectangle. Draw and Type provide alternatives when you do not already have an image.
steps: Open Sign PDF and choose the document. Check its filename and page count.
Choose Draw, Type or Upload. For drawing, set pen color and width, then clear or undo strokes until satisfied.
Add the mark to the page. Drag it into position, resize it and use rotation or alignment controls as needed.
Choose the current page, all pages or a range such as 1,3-5,last. Confirm that the preview shows the intended pages.
Download the edited PDF and open it to check every required signature placement.

sections.heading: Work accurately at different zoom levels
paragraphs: Use the thumbnail rail to move to the correct page, then zoom in to inspect a signature line. Zoom changes your view; it should not change the signature's intended page position. Mixed portrait and landscape documents deserve a check on each page orientation.

If you place a mark on all pages and then move it on one page, review the application controls before assuming that every other placement has changed. Use the preview and apply action deliberately rather than relying on an unstated repetition rule.

sections.heading: Save only what you want to reuse
paragraphs: The reusable signature library is optional and stored in this browser. Leave saving off on a shared computer. Remove PDF clears the active document, while Forget saved images clears reusable assets; they are separate controls.

If export uses compatibility rendering for an encrypted or incompatible source, affected pages become images. Inspect readability and placement in the downloaded result. A file that asks for an opening password needs an authorized unlocked copy first.

faq.q: Can I sign using a finger or pen?
faq.a: The Draw control accepts supported touch or pointer input. Make a short test stroke, adjust the width and review the mark before placing it.

faq.q: Is a typed name a digital certificate signature?
faq.a: No. It is a visual text mark. The tool does not verify identity or create a cryptographic signature.

guides/stamp-pdf.title: How to add a stamp to PDF pages
guides/stamp-pdf.description: Place a stamp image on one page or repeat it across a chosen page range.

sections.heading: Choose a clear stamp image
paragraphs: A stamp can be a department mark, review label, company seal or other image you are authorized to use. A transparent PNG usually blends best with the document. Crop unused space around the artwork before placing it so the visible mark is easy to size.
A stamp image does not prove approval or authorization. Use the correct wording and obtain permission before applying a company or another person's mark.
steps: Open the PDF in Sign PDF and add the stamp through Upload, or choose a reusable saved image.
Select the stamp in the image library. Drag it to an uncluttered part of the target page.
Resize and, if needed, rotate it. Check that it does not cover required text, signatures or barcodes.
Apply it to the current page, all pages or selected ranges. Use the all-images option only when you intend to apply the signature and stamp together.
Inspect the affected pages using thumbnails and download a new PDF.

sections.heading: Repeat placement across different page sizes
paragraphs: A repeated placement uses the document's page geometry. Check at least one portrait page, one landscape page and any unusual-sized pages before exporting a mixed document. A relative corner position can be useful, but a large stamp can still cover content on a smaller page.

The active selection matters when several signatures and stamps are loaded. Select the correct image before resizing or applying a range. Use Delete on an unwanted placement rather than clearing the entire workspace.

sections.heading: Reuse and troubleshooting
paragraphs: Opt in to saving only if you want the stamp available in this browser next time. Browser storage is local to the browser profile and is not a protected company asset repository. Forget saved images on shared devices.

If the stamp has a white background, use a transparent source rather than assuming the PDF editor can recover hidden page text beneath it. If a PDF cannot be copied directly, recovery may flatten affected pages into images; verify the final appearance before sharing.

faq.q: Can a signature and stamp be exported together?
faq.a: Yes. Add both images, place each one and apply them as required. Review the all-images option before applying both to a range.

faq.q: Can I use a JPG stamp?
faq.a: Yes, but JPG does not preserve transparency. A white background in the source image will remain visible.

guides/merge-pdf.title: How to merge PDFs and images in your own order
guides/merge-pdf.description: Combine files, organize individual pages and understand compatibility recovery.

sections.heading: Build a list before creating the output
paragraphs: Merge PDF accepts PDF documents and supported image files in one workspace. Each file becomes an item that can be expanded into individual pages. The final PDF follows the visible arrangement, so organize the list before exporting.
The merge list is retained in this browser's IndexedDB storage. That is useful when you refresh, but it also means source files can remain on a shared device until you clear the saved workspace.
steps: Open Merge PDF and choose the source PDFs or JPG, PNG and WebP images.
Arrange file items using drag handles or movement controls. Expand an item to inspect its pages.
Select pages to group, reorder, rotate, duplicate or remove. Use undo when a recent arrangement change was unintended.
Choose an output name and the image page-size options. Confirm the total page count and order.
Create the PDF, wait for completion and open the download to review its first, last and any rearranged pages.

sections.heading: When a PDF displays but cannot merge normally
paragraphs: Some encrypted PDFs open without an opening password but cannot be copied by the PDF-writing library. The merge recovery path can render those pages from the local preview. The completion notice identifies how many pages were exported as images.

Compatibility mode renders all PDF pages as images when direct copying remains unreliable. It preserves visible page appearance and order, but can increase file size and removes selectable text and interactive page behavior. It does not bypass an opening password.

sections.heading: Large groups and safe cleanup
paragraphs: The configured merge input limit is 400 MB, with a 100 MB per-file limit and a 1,500-page limit. Browser memory can still run out on smaller inputs, especially with large scans. Close unnecessary tabs or split a very large job into smaller batches if processing stalls.

Remove everything clears the saved merge workspace; it is not required to retry a download. Keep originals and completed downloads separately. On a shared device, clear the retained merge files when you have finished.

faq.q: Does grouping pages download them immediately?
faq.a: Grouping organizes the workspace. Use Create PDF or the relevant download action to produce an output file.

faq.q: Can I mix scans and text PDFs?
faq.a: Yes, supported image files and PDFs can be combined. Recovery may flatten incompatible PDF pages, while directly copied pages can retain their existing text layer.

guides/split-pdf.title: How to split or extract PDF pages
guides/split-pdf.description: Create a smaller PDF from selected pages or divide a document into downloadable parts.

sections.heading: Choose extraction or splitting
paragraphs: Extracting collects selected pages into a new PDF. Splitting creates separate outputs, such as one file per page or one file for every chosen number of pages. Decide which result you need before exporting so you do not create hundreds of files unintentionally.
Page references are based on the PDF's physical page positions, starting at 1. A printed page label on the document may be different, especially when cover sheets or appendices are present.
steps: Open Split PDF or Extract Pages and load the document.
Review the thumbnails and enter an inclusive range such as 1,3-5,last, or choose the split interval.
Check the resulting page selection and number of output files.
Export the selected PDF or download the ZIP when several outputs are created.
Open the result and verify the first and last page of each section before sharing it.

sections.heading: Keep the intended order
paragraphs: Use the preview to distinguish a page number printed on a sheet from its position in the PDF. Check a boundary page when splitting at a chapter or tender section. A range such as 3-5 includes pages 3, 4 and 5.

For reordering, duplicate pages or inserted blanks, use Organize Pages before splitting. Undo and redo apply to supported workspace changes, but they do not recall files that have already been downloaded or sent elsewhere.

sections.heading: Quality and compatibility
paragraphs: Direct extraction preserves the original PDF page contents and selectable text when the source supports copying. Incompatible or encrypted sources may need image recovery, which changes text selection and interactive elements. The result should be reviewed like any rebuilt PDF.

The tools do not perform OCR, remove opening passwords or convert a PDF into an editable Word document. For a scanned document, extracting a page keeps the scan; it does not turn the printed words into a text layer.

faq.q: Why is my output a ZIP?
faq.a: A ZIP keeps several split PDFs together in one download. Extract the archive using your operating system before opening or sharing the individual PDFs.

faq.q: Does splitting change the source file?
faq.a: The tool generates new output files. The original file on your device is not overwritten.

guides/page-numbers.title: How to add page numbers to a PDF
guides/page-numbers.description: Set a starting number, choose pages and position the numbering consistently.

sections.heading: Separate document position from printed numbering
paragraphs: The PDF viewer counts physical pages from 1, but the number printed on a page can start elsewhere. For example, you might leave a cover unnumbered and print 1 on the second PDF page. Decide this rule before applying numbers.
Use a margin that keeps the numbering inside the visible page while avoiding existing footers, stamps or signatures. Landscape and mixed-size pages need a quick preview check.
steps: Open Page Numbers and choose your PDF.
Enable numbering and choose the page range or exclusions, including whether a cover should be skipped.
Set the starting number, format, position, font size and margin.
Inspect the first numbered page, a middle page and the last numbered page using the viewer.
Download the edited PDF and confirm the numbering sequence in the output.

sections.heading: Formats and ranges
paragraphs: A simple sequence is useful for a working copy. A format such as Page 1 of 10 can be clearer for a packet that will be printed or sent separately. Check how the selected start value and page range affect the last printed number rather than assuming it equals the original document's page count.

Use ranges such as 1,3-5,last only when those physical PDF positions match your intent. If the source already contains printed page numbers, the new numbers are added to the page; they do not erase the originals.

sections.heading: Review and privacy
paragraphs: The PDF stays in browser memory while you edit. Replacing the document resets document-specific placements and numbering, so check the settings on the new file. Remove PDF is separate from clearing retained merge data or reusable signatures.

Adding page numbers modifies the PDF and can invalidate an existing cryptographic signature. If recovery is required for an incompatible source, affected pages can become image-based. Keep the original and review the download before using it as an official record.

faq.q: Can I leave a cover page unnumbered?
faq.a: Yes. Start numbering on the required PDF page or exclude the cover using the range controls, then check the preview.

faq.q: Will numbering remove old page numbers?
faq.a: No. It adds new page content. Existing printed numbers remain unless changed in a separate appropriate editing workflow.

guides/images-to-pdf.title: How to convert images into a PDF
guides/images-to-pdf.description: Arrange JPG, PNG and WebP files and choose page size, fit, orientation and margins.

sections.heading: Prepare readable source images
paragraphs: Use images that are sharp enough to read at the intended page size. Converting a low-resolution photograph to a large PDF page cannot restore missing detail. Crop irrelevant surroundings and check that text is upright before building a document.
JPG is common for scans and photographs; PNG is useful for graphics and transparency; WebP is also supported. A PDF created from images is image-based and does not gain searchable text automatically.
steps: Open Images to PDF and select the JPG, PNG or WebP files.
Arrange the images in the order they should appear. Check filenames and thumbnails rather than relying on the file picker's selection order.
Choose A4, Letter or original dimensions, then set orientation, margins and fit or fill.
Review the preview. Fit retains the full image with possible whitespace; fill can crop edges to cover the chosen page area.
Create the PDF and inspect text clarity, page edges and orientation in the download.

sections.heading: Choose fit and page size deliberately
paragraphs: A4 and Letter create consistent page dimensions for printing or document packets. Original size follows the source image dimensions and can produce a mixed-size PDF. A landscape choice is useful for wide charts or horizontal photographs.

Margins provide space around the image, but larger margins also reduce its visible size on a fixed page. When using fill, check that signatures, page numbers, QR codes and text near an image's edges have not been cropped.

sections.heading: File size and limitations
paragraphs: High-resolution images can create a large PDF and use substantial browser memory. The configured per-file limit is 100 MB; available device memory may become the practical limit earlier. A lower-resolution source may be sufficient for screen use, while small text can need more detail.

The tools process image contents locally. If you add images through the merge workspace, that workspace retains its source bytes in this browser until cleared. The conversion does not provide OCR, certify a scanned document or replace the original image files.

faq.q: Why can't I select text in the new PDF?
faq.a: The pages contain images. Text recognition requires OCR, which is not included in this release.

faq.q: What is the difference between fit and fill?
faq.a: Fit keeps the entire image visible, with whitespace if its proportions differ from the page. Fill covers the chosen area and can crop the image edges.
